_comment: THE single source for every origin, CSP value and CORS value in this project.
CLAUDE.md section 2: 'keep every origin/CSP/CORS value in one config module so it is a
one-file change later.' This is that file. `_headers` and assets/js/config.js are both
GENERATED from it by scripts/build-site-config.mjs, and CI regenerates them and fails on
any diff -- so 'one-file change' is enforced rather than promised.
To point the project at a real domain: edit `domains` here, run the generator, commit.
Nothing else in the repository should ever contain a hostname.
_domains_comment: r2_s3 is the R2 S3 API endpoint, and it is here because the UPLOAD PUT goes straight
to it from the browser: request-upload presigns against this host (sigv4.ts builds it
from R2_ACCOUNT_ID), and the XHR in upload.js sends the bytes there directly.
connect-src must therefore admit it, or the page's own CSP blocks the PUT before CORS
is ever consulted -- which is exactly what it did from M1 until 29 Aug 2026. The
symptom was upload.js's generic offline message, and nothing in it named the CSP.
This is NOT the same host as cdn. Reads come from the r2.dev public bucket; writes go
to the S3 API. Two hosts, two directions, and the CSP needs both.
THE ACCOUNT ID IS IN THIS FILE ON PURPOSE, and it is the one value here that was
argued about. It is not capability-bearing -- R2 authorises by signature, not by
account id -- and every uploading member already receives it inside the presigned URL,
so it cannot be withheld from the people who use the site. The exact host is preferred
over a *.r2.cloudflarestorage.com wildcard because a wildcard would make ANY R2
account a destination this page may send data to, which is a real widening of an
otherwise tight connect-src. The narrow value is the safer one here, not merely the
The R2 access key and secret remain what section 6 is about, and neither is here.
_supabase_comment: The anon key, which section 6 draws a line under explicitly: 'The Supabase anon key is
designed to be public and is not the concern; the service-role key, any third-party API
key, and any admin credential are.' It ships to every visitor in assets/js/config.js,
exactly like the Turnstile site key beside it. .gitleaks.toml already carved it out of
the generic `jwt` rule for this moment.
It is EMPTY until the hosted key is pasted in. Empty is deliberate rather than a
placeholder string: the generator refuses to emit anything that is not an anon token,
and auth.js throws a named error rather than sending unauthenticated requests that fail
The generator DECODES this and refuses any token whose role claim is not 'anon'. That
check is the point of the field being here at all — the field a service-role key gets
pasted into by mistake is the field next to the word 'supabase' in a config file.
_turnstile_comment: Cloudflare Turnstile — section 6 requires it on signup and submit.
site_key is PUBLIC by design. It is embedded in the page markup for every visitor to
read, exactly like the Supabase anon key, and it is not a capability: it identifies
the widget, it does not authorise anything. The SECRET key is the capability-bearing
half, it verifies the token server-side, and it must never appear in this repository
-- it belongs in GitHub Actions secrets and the Edge Function environment only.
There is deliberately no field for it here, not even an empty one, because an empty
WIRED, M1 piece 4. The origin moved out of this block and into `domains` as
`turnstile`, which is what lets `csp` reference it as @turnstile in script-src and
frame-src -- and, just as importantly, what stops the origin ratchet in
scripts/frontend-csp-test.mjs reading the widget script in index.html as an
undeclared third-party origin. It is now a declared one, allowed on purpose.
Both directives are needed and neither is redundant: script-src admits the widget's
own JS, frame-src admits the challenge iframe it creates. Allow only the first and
the widget loads and then silently fails to render.
_function_cors_comment: CORS allowlist for the Edge Functions -- today just request-upload (M1).
Section 2 keeps every origin in this file, but an Edge Function is deployed separately
from the site and cannot read config/site.json at runtime. So the function reads the
environment variable UPLOAD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, and the generator prints the exact
`supabase secrets set` line to copy. This file stays authoritative; the secret is
only its deployment. That is a real seam -- nothing can prove the hosted secret still
matches this list -- so re-run the generator and re-set the secret in the same breath.
STAGING ONLY. No production custom domain is provisioned yet, so PLACEHOLDER_DOMAIN is
deliberately not expanded into this list: `https://PLACEHOLDER_DOMAIN` is not an origin
any browser will ever send, and the generator refuses it rather than shipping a line
that looks configured and matches nothing.
The localhost entry is http, not https, and is the one value here that would be a
defect on a live site -- a plain-http origin in a CORS allowlist is reachable by
anyone who can spoof http on the network. It is acceptable only because this list is
staging: when the production origin is added it REPLACES these two rather than
_read_path_comment: Where the browser fetches the archive from -- section 2's read path: manifest.json, then
feed/, item/, decade/, geo/, profile/ and content.json under /v/{ts}/, then redactions.json.
The publisher writes all of it into the R2 `public` bucket, which is CDN-fronted, so
@cdn is the value that matches the deployment CLAUDE.md describes. `self` is the other
legitimate value -- it means the release tree is served from the Pages origin itself, and
it is what site/_headers already writes cache rules for. Either way it is ONE token here
rather than a hostname in the front end.
connect-src must admit whatever this resolves to. @cdn is already in the list.
IF YOU SET THIS TO `self`, the release tree has to be IN the Pages output directory.
site/_redirects ends with `/*  /index.html  200`, and Pages serves a real file before it
consults that rule -- so a manifest.json that is not there comes back as the SPA shell
with a 200, and archive.js reports a malformed archive rather than a missing one. The
publisher writes to R2, so `self` means something has to sync it across.
_basemap_comment: M4's basemap. CLAUDE.md section 2: 'PMTiles (Palestine extract) on R2. NEVER the public
OSM tile endpoint.' One object in the `public` bucket, read with HTTP Range requests, so
it arrives over the same CDN as the shards at the same $0 egress and there is no tile
server to run, rate-limit or pay for.
`path` is relative to read_path.base, exactly like every shard path -- it is NOT a URL,
for the same reason nothing else in the front end carries a hostname.
EMPTY until the extract is built and uploaded. Empty is deliberate and is not a failure:
map.js is only fetched when there is a basemap to draw, so an empty value renders /map as
the list view -- which is section 10's own stated tile-failure fallback, reached by the
same path a broken archive reaches it by. See the README for the one command that builds
`attribution` is a legal requirement rather than a courtesy: a Protomaps extract is
derived from OpenStreetMap, whose licence requires the credit to be displayed. It is
rendered as text beside the map, in both languages, and it is here rather than in i18n.js
because it is a property of the FILE -- change the extract's source and this changes with
_function_env_comment: Values a deployed Edge Function needs that are not origins in the CORS sense. Same seam
as function_cors above and the same mitigation: the generator prints the exact
`supabase secrets set` line on every run, because nothing here can read the hosted value
back and confirm it still matches.
site_origin is where a prerendered item page says it lives -- the canonical link, the
og:url, and the base for og:image. It has to be an absolute origin because a crawler
resolves nothing: WhatsApp fetches the URL it was given and reads the tags verbatim.
STAGING ONLY, exactly like function_cors. PLACEHOLDER_DOMAIN is not an origin any
crawler will resolve, so the staging Pages origin is the honest value until a production
domain is provisioned -- at which point it REPLACES this rather than joining it.
_csp_comment: No 'unsafe-inline' and no 'unsafe-eval' anywhere -- section 6. @tokens resolve to
default-src 'none' means every directive not listed below is DENIED, so adding a new
kind of subresource is a deliberate edit here rather than something that silently works.
form-action 'none': nothing in this app submits an HTML form. Supabase Auth is fetch().
Set to 'none' rather than 'self' because the attack it stops is an injected <form> that
POSTs a password somewhere else, and 'self' does not stop that being staged.
_headers_comment: Referrer-Policy is no-referrer, not the usual strict-origin-when-cross-origin. This is a
politically sensitive archive (section 7); an outbound link should not tell the
destination which page of it the reader came from.
Permissions-Policy: microphone is allowed for 'self' because voice notes are a first-class
content type and M1 may record in-browser. Camera and geolocation are denied outright --
nothing in CLAUDE.md asks for either, and device geolocation on a heritage map is a

headers.Permissions-Policy: accelerometer=(), camera=(), geolocation=(), gyroscope=(), magnetometer=(), payment=(), usb=(), microphone=(self)

_known_violations_comment: External origins the prototype front end still loads, every one of which this CSP BLOCKS
and CLAUDE.md already forbids. Listed here so CI can ratchet: a new external origin fails
the build, and removing one requires deleting its line, which is the point.
None of these break anything today -- `_headers` is a Cloudflare Pages file and the site
is not on Cloudflare Pages yet. They break the moment it is. That is deliberate: it makes
M4 and M6 unable to ship without doing what CLAUDE.md already requires.
_known_violations_now_empty: Both entries were the Google Fonts origins, and both were removed on 1 Sep 2026 by M6's
font subsetting: the two families are self-hosted, subsetted and unicode-range split
under site/assets/fonts/, generated by scripts/subset-fonts.py. The list is EMPTY and
that is the state to keep it in -- the ratchet exists so adding an external origin has
to be an argument somebody writes down, not a <link> somebody pastes.
